key_finding: Intuitive Machines' counterparty map is dominated by NASA. The Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program is the single most consequential customer relationship — a $4.82B contract ceiling with multiple task orders awarded under it. Secondary government customers include DoD, DARPA, Space Force. The Lanteris acquisition diversifies the customer mix by adding satellite-systems customers in commercial and government markets. The competitive set in lunar delivery is Astrobotic (also a CLPS awardee, conducted unsuccessful Peregrine lunar landing attempt), Firefly Aerospace (also CLPS, achieved successful Blue Ghost landing), and to a less direct extent SpaceX and Blue Origin who provide launch services rather than payload delivery.

im5_task_order.scope: Deliver seven science and technology payloads to the Lunar South Pole using cargo-class Nova-D lander

nasa_clps_program.framing: CLPS is NASA's commercial procurement program for lunar payload delivery services. Intuitive Machines, Firefly, Astrobotic, and a handful of others are competing for task orders within the program. CLPS is structurally similar to Commercial Resupply Services (CRS) and Commercial Crew (CCP) that funded SpaceX's early commercial development.

lunar_missions.outcome: First private company to successfully land a spacecraft on the Moon's surface (touchdown achieved despite landing-leg complications and a sideways resting orientation)
Reached lunar surface; mission outcome had operational complications similar to IM-1

primary_customers.name: NASA Artemis program
primary_customers.type: Adjacent government customer for lunar infrastructure

competitive_set.name: Astrobotic Technology
competitive_set.framing: Private CLPS awardee; conducted unsuccessful Peregrine lunar landing attempt in 2024 (mission ended before reaching lunar surface)

competitive_set.name: Firefly Aerospace
competitive_set.framing: Public via FLY ticker; conducted successful Blue Ghost lunar landing in 2025

competitive_set.name: SpaceX
competitive_set.framing: Launch services provider; not directly competing in lunar payload delivery but provides Starship as the broader lunar transportation platform via NASA HLS

competitive_set.name: Blue Origin
competitive_set.framing: Launch services + lunar landing development (Blue Moon); the NASA HLS sustained lunar lander competitor

competitive_set.name: Lockheed Martin / Northrop Grumman / Boeing / Raytheon
competitive_set.framing: Traditional aerospace and defense primes; competitive overlap on broader space-systems and NASA contract work, especially post-Lanteris acquisition

supply_chain_observations.lander_propulsion: Intuitive Machines designs and builds its own Nova-C and Nova-D lander platforms in Houston
supply_chain_observations.launch_services: IM-1 launched on SpaceX Falcon 9. Subsequent missions also expected on SpaceX or potentially Blue Origin New Glenn
supply_chain_observations.ground_systems: Lunar Telemetry, Tracking, and Control (TT&C) capability is one of IM's proprietary capabilities — could become a separate revenue line

lanteris_acquisition_counterparty_additi: The $800M Lanteris acquisition (expected close Q1 2026) adds a satellite-systems customer book that brings Intuitive Machines into competitive overlap with the traditional aerospace primes on broader space-systems contracts. Lanteris CEO Chris Johnson (now President of Lanteris within IM) brings Boeing Satellite Systems International institutional relationships.
